subject: TTFT & streaming: cadence options, SLA budget and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Markova <elena@finserv.io>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vikram Patel <vikram@finserv.io>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro & performance goals — quick follow-up

Thanks for the call this morning, Jasmine. Quick clarifications from our side to help you size things: 

- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token): 120-180 ms p95 for single-turn username -> model reply in our EU region (we know you'll have routing options).
- Sustained throughput: ~12k tokens/sec average during peak batch windows (approx 1.2k requests/minute, average 100 tokens per request).
- Concurrency: expect bursts to 110 concurrent streaming sessions; steady-state concurrency around 35.
- Streaming requirements: Browser-based UI will subscribe via SSE if stable; mobile app prefers WebSocket. We need the server to support both and be able to set chunk cadence independently.

For chunk cadence we prefer 200-400 ms chunks for conversational feel, but we'll consider 500 ms if that significantly lowers cost.

I'll attach our raw telemetry sample and a small request trace (see 2026-08-05-ttft-profiles.csv). Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet 150 ms p95 + support SSE + WS with independent chunk cadence control?

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
FinServ Analytics

Attachment: 2026-08-05-ttft-profiles.csv (csv, 48KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Markova <elena@finserv.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming: cadence options, SLA budget and next steps

Elena — thanks for the detailed numbers and the sample traces, that's very helpful. High-level response and proposed next steps below.

Summary of feasibility (short):
- TTFT: We can target 150 ms p95 for your EU traffic with a Dedicated pool sized for your steady-state concurrency (35) plus burst capacity (110). We typically guarantee p95 SLAs via Dedicated or a Dedicated-backed routing policy.
- Throughput: 12k tokens/sec is within the expected output for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with continuous batching; we will validate with a controlled pilot.
- Concurrency & bursts: autoscaling with pre-warmed standby capacity + a small burst headroom policy should cover 110 concurrent streaming sessions without violating TTFT targets.
- SSE vs WS: Redwood supports both SSE and WebSocket. SSE is slightly cheaper for browser-only consumption (no connection handshake costs), but WebSocket gives lower tail variance for stateful mobile sessions. We can expose both endpoints; cadence control is per-route.

Trade-offs (concrete):
- More aggressive chunk cadence (100-200 ms) increases per-token overhead and may raise unit cost by ~8-12% relative to 300-400 ms cadence.
- Accepting 300-500 ms cadence typically reduces cost while preserving UX for longer responses.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Engineering pilot: Redwood runs a 72-hour pilot against a shadow subset (we replay your sample trace) to validate TTFT and token throughput with two cadence configs (250 ms and 400 ms). (Rishi to lead.)
2) SLA proposal & quote: We'll produce a Dedicated sizing + cost model and SLA draft based on pilot results. (Marissa to prepare.)
3) Joint test: If pilot looks good, schedule a 2-week production pilot with canary routing and fallbacks.

Questions for you:
- Can you provide a short list of 10 representative API calls (we'll use them in the pilot)?
- Any hard requirement on p99 latency or cold-start constraints?

I'll attach a short playbook (chunking-playbook-v1.pdf) that explains cadence options and measurable impacts. Suggest we sync again after pilot kickoff to review results.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: chunking-playbook-v1.pdf, proposal-draft-FS-2026-08.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Markova <elena@finserv.io>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming: cadence options, SLA budget and next steps

Elena, thanks — this is actionable. A few engineering notes and what we'll validate during the 72-hour replay: 

Pilot validation targets (what we'll measure):
- p95 TTFT target: <= 150 ms (we'll measure server-side and end-to-end from your EU vantage).
- p99 TTFT: report as advisory, expect ~2x p95 without dedicated kernel tuning; we can try quantization variants to compress tail.
- Throughput: sustain >= 12k tokens/sec for 6-minute windows with <5% error budget on token completion.
- Concurrent SSE sessions: test up to 120 sessions with mixed SSE/WS ratio 70/30.
- Chunk cadence experiments: compare 250 ms vs 400 ms; measure perceived latency (time to first chunk) and cost delta.

Operational notes:
- We'll enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts to reduce TTFT for similar queries. Please confirm if prompt templating will be used heavily (helps caching).
- For SSE we recommend a 2-second keepalive ping and a chunk-aggregation option for small tokens to avoid many tiny network frames.

Logistics:
- Please drop the 10 representative calls into the shared Drive link by EOD Friday.
- We'll provision the Dedicated pilot cluster in eu-west-1 and share access details.

I'll run the replay and post preliminary results to the HubSpot deal record and the shared Drive folder.

-Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quoted attachments: none

Thanks — all clear and appreciated. We uploaded the 10 representative calls to the Drive link and granted read access to rishi@redwood.ai. Minor clarifications: 

- We will heavily use prompt templates for KYC flows (good news for caching).
- p99 is important for compliance audits; if the pilot shows p99 > 600 ms we will request a follow-up plan for tail improvements.
- For the pilot please enable detailed token-level billing so we can evaluate cost impact per cadence.

Let's aim to start the 72-hour pilot on Monday 2026-08-10; can you confirm provisioning timeline?

Elena
